name: Text selection and caret
plain: Lets the page see what is selected inside itself and move the cursor; nothing outside the page.
meaning: A site knows which of its own words the person highlights, which reveals interest and reading focus. It cannot see a selection in another tab or app.

access.persistence: Live while the page has focus
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Frames see only their own selection; selection in a cross-origin iframe is hidden from the parent
steps: Page reads the Selection and Range

limits.headline: Can see which of its own words you highlight and move your text cursor
limits.user_action: You highlight text or click in a box on the page
can: See the text you select on the page
Move the cursor or change the selection on its own page
Guess what you are interested in from what you highlight
cannot: See selections in other tabs or apps
See what you select when the page is in the background
Show a permission pop up; there is none
limits.reach_label: Only text on its own page

story.what_it_is: The page sees which of its own words you highlight and where your text cursor is.
story.for_you: You highlight text to copy, look up or share. A small menu may pop up near it. You did not know the page could tell which words you picked. It cannot see selections in other tabs or apps.
story.for_makers: Makers use selection to show a share, quote or highlight menu. Reading apps remember highlights and analytics tools learn what people find interesting.

use_cases.example: A long read site shows a 'share this quote' button when a reader highlights a sentence.
An e-reader or course page saves a student's highlights and notes for later.
A document editor uses selection to show a bold or link toolbar.
A word game or learning site checks which word a player picked from a passage.
A publisher counts which lines get highlighted most to see what resonates.
A dictionary or search widget can show an ad or lookup for the exact words you picked.

technical_bounds: Sees selection inside its own document (and same-origin frames) only
Cannot read the selection from the address bar, other tabs, other apps or browser UI
Password fields: selected text of a password input is not exposed by getSelection().toString() but is readable via the field's value to the page owner
selectionchange has no rate limit; it can fire many times per second while dragging
Firefox returns the selection inside inputs only through selectionStart and selectionEnd
